brief.headline: Push for a 5–8% price cut and 30-day payment — they keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% typical, so there's room

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 5–8% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Aim for ₹0.65–0.80/pc on caps (market says this is possible at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 8.5% of sales as profit, well above the 4.8% that similar firms keep. The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, and the market verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'. Their margin cushion and the market band both support our target.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹2.15 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: They're financially safe — score 6.18 on the distress scale (safe zone), zero debt, and they keep 8.5% profit. But their cash is stuck for 124 days, longer than similar firms at 114 days, and they show negative free cash flow of ₹-6.59 Cr, so cash is a bit tight for them. We're tiny to them at ₹26.17 L — just 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue — so on our own we have little pull. That means we need to bundle volume, commit longer, or play them against one of the strong alternates to get traction.

evidence.point: They keep 8.5% of sales as profit, much better than the 4.8% similar firms keep
Their cash is stuck for 124 days, longer than the 114 days typical for similar firms
They show negative free cash flow
We are a very small customer — just 0.15% of everything they sell
Market ask for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
Moving to 30-day payment terms would free up cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — strong, profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures

risks: We're only 0.15% of their business, so they can easily walk away — bundle more volume or commit for a longer term to get leverage
They have an EPF payment delay flag, so watch for any operational hiccups that could hit our supply
Their negative free cash flow of ₹-6.59 Cr means cash is tight despite zero debt — don't push so hard that you spook them into prioritizing bigger customers
We have no internal best-price or SKU-level gap data for rigid plastic packaging, so lean on the market ask and the alternates to anchor the price discussion
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to lock in a multi-year commitment with you, but we need your price to land in the ₹0.65–0.80 band the market shows for higher-volume cap orders, and we'd like 30-day terms to match how you pay your own suppliers.
